answer: Each agent identity must periodically complete a unique, non-parallelizable compute puzzle bound to its public key, like climbing a summit that cannot be shortcut. A sybil attacker faces the same umber cost per fake identity, so ten thousand sockpuppets cost ten thousand puzzles while one honest agent pays once. The work is verifiable on-chain, expires, and cannot be reused across identities, so the meadow of cheap fake accounts dries up: scale itself becomes the attacker's tax.
